patch.value: Allow linked tests to opt out of source-workspace injection for self-sandboxing repo-wide gates

pm test always exports PM_SOURCE_WORKSPACE_ROOT in schema, tracker, and auto modes. Repo-wide test runners that intentionally create their own isolated PM roots therefore change file-governance and merge-receipt semantics when linked, even though the identical direct gate passes.

A documented linked-test context mode or scoped safe control can omit source-workspace injection without allowing PM_PATH or PM_GLOBAL_PATH escape; repo-wide run-tests coverage passes both directly and as a linked test; execution_context reports the opt-out explicitly
Preserve protected tracker-root isolation and add adversarial tests proving linked metadata cannot override protected paths.
pm test linked runner wrapping node scripts/run-tests.mjs coverage

Link node scripts/run-tests.mjs coverage to an item and run pm test <id> --run; validate file-governance tests scan PM_SOURCE_WORKSPACE_ROOT and fail, while the same command directly passes 100/100/100/100.
A self-sandboxing repository gate can be recorded and executed through pm without inherited source-workspace semantics.
All supported modes inject PM_SOURCE_WORKSPACE_ROOT; auto resolves to schema for non-PM commands and protected env directives cannot clear it.
Agents cannot record certain authoritative whole-repository gates as passing linked evidence without changing their semantics.
